name: Moped
description: The lowest-powered motor driven cycle: a motor of 2 brake horsepower (1,492 W) or less that can reach between 20 and 30 mph within a mile, with or without pedals. An electric motor qualifies on power alone; the 50 cc limit applies only to combustion engines. Defined by Illinois Vehicle Code §1-148.2 (625 ILCS 5/1-148.2).
restrictions: A motor driven cycle, with or without pedals, whose motor produces 2 brake horsepower (1,492 W) or less
The speed it can reach within one mile is at least 20 mph and no more than 30 mph
Doesn't make the rider shift gears; failing any of these criteria makes it a motor driven cycle that needs a Class L license
Riders need a valid driver's license of any classification; no motorcycle classification is needed
Rider and passenger must wear glasses, goggles or a face shield unless it has a windshield that rises above the rider's eyes
Titled and registered with the Secretary of State, carries a license plate, and must carry liability insurance
Carries a passenger only if built for two, with a passenger seat and footrests
The Department of Transportation may bar motor driven cycles, mopeds included, from controlled access highways it signs
From January 1, 2027, as a motor driven cycle it may not be ridden on sidewalks, bike lanes, bicycle paths, shared-use paths, bike trails or interstate highways
